key_insight: Brain-SAD adds a dynamic, brain-inspired fear signal to switch between long-term driving and short-term collision-defense policies, making safety constraints adapt to the current traffic scene.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous driving systems, this suggests a more robust way to enforce safety online by coupling policy optimization with context-dependent risk and feasible-action boundaries.
method: Perceives the current vehicle-interaction scene to generate a dynamic fear signal.
Uses two policies: a regular interaction policy and an urgent-collision-defense policy.
Constructs dynamic fear constraints that shape both action cost and feasible-region boundary during online optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved success rate, shorter task-completion and collision-recovery time, and stronger reliability across intersections with varying complexity.
watch_item: The approach may be more complex to deploy because its dynamic fear signal and risk boundary estimation must remain stable and accurate across diverse real-world driving scenes.
paper_title: Brain-SAD: A Brain-Inspired Safe Autonomous Driving Control Framework with Dynamic Fear-Oriented Constraint on Dual-Policy
